introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2019. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Layout of the paper: Section A, Map Work (question 1, the only question of its section); Section B, Physical Geography (questions 2 and 3); Section C, Human Geography (questions 4 and 5); Section D, Cameroon Geography (questions 6 and 7).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) You have visited a coastal area, desert, landscape and a river course and studied their features.

(i) On a table, list two features found on each of the areas.

(ii) Show the appearance of any two features using diagrams.

(iii) Explain the formation of one of the features drawn in (a)(ii) above.

(3 + 4 + 3 = 10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Table of features**

| Coastal area | Desert landscape | River course |
|---|---|---|
| Cliff | Sand dune | Waterfall |
| Wave-cut platform | Inselberg (isolated rock hill) | Meander |

(Other valid features: coastal - beach, spit, stack, arch, bay; desert - wadi, mesa, butte, pediment; river - V-shaped valley, flood plain, ox-bow lake, delta.) One mark for each correct pair, up to three.

**(ii) Diagrams.** Two features are drawn: a cliff with its wave-cut platform (coast) and a meander (river).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2019-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

The diagrams must be large, drawn in pencil, with a title and labels (cliff, notch, platform, sea level; outer bank or river cliff, inner bank or slip-off slope, direction of flow).

**(iii) Formation of a cliff and wave-cut platform.**

1. Waves break against the base of a rock coast between high and low tide. They attack the rock by hydraulic action (the force of water and of compressed air in cracks), abrasion (rocks and sand thrown against the cliff) and solution (in limestone).
2. The attack is strongest at the foot of the rock, so a **wave-cut notch** is cut at the base of the cliff.
3. The rock above the notch is no longer supported; it cracks and collapses, so the cliff face becomes steep and **retreats inland**.
4. The collapsed material is broken up by the waves and carried away. The rock surface left behind at the foot of the cliff, between high and low tide, is a **gently sloping, flat rocky platform**, the wave-cut platform.
5. As the cliff retreats again and again, the platform becomes wider.

(Alternative: the formation of a meander - the river flows faster and erodes the outer bank of a bend, forming a river cliff, and drops its load on the slow inner bank, forming a slip-off slope, so the bend becomes larger over time.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Give four characteristics of the tropical rain forest that makes it different from other vegetation types.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Tall evergreen trees**: they keep their leaves all year and reach great heights (commonly 40 m or more), with no season when all trees lose their leaves.
2. **Layers (storeys)**: the forest has several layers: emergent trees, a dense closed canopy, an understorey of smaller trees and a shrub layer; the canopy blocks the sunlight, so little grows on the ground.
3. **Great variety of species**: many different tree species grow side by side (unlike a coniferous forest, which has a few species in pure stands); the trees are mainly hardwoods.
4. **Special features of the plants**: broad leaves with pointed drip tips, buttress roots, climbers (lianas) and plants growing on branches (epiphytes).

One mark for each characteristic clearly stated.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Describe two ways by which man can reduce the effects of each of the following:

(i) Global warming.

(ii) Water erosion.

(iii) Earthquakes.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Global warming**

1. Reduce the burning of fossil fuels (coal, oil and gas) by using cleaner, renewable energy: solar, wind, hydro-electric power and biogas.
2. Stop deforestation and plant trees (afforestation), since trees take carbon dioxide out of the air. (Also: save energy, and follow international agreements on emissions.)

**(ii) Water erosion**

1. Farm in ways that slow the water on slopes: plough along the contours, build terraces and plant grass strips.
2. Keep the soil covered with vegetation: plant trees (afforestation), use cover crops and mulch, and avoid overgrazing.

**(iii) Earthquakes**

1. Build earthquake-resistant buildings (strong, flexible frames) and do not build on weak ground or on fault lines.
2. Monitor earthquake zones, prepare people with drills and public education, and organize emergency services and shelters.

One mark for each way clearly described (two for each of the three effects).
